The release where RoboInvestor becomes the public home for company research. Since v0.4.0, roboinvestor.ai has taken over the research pages from robosystems.ai and gained a page for every SEC filer, built from the filing itself. Inside the app, **Company Research** replaces the old SEC filing viewer and needs no graph selected, and you can put a question to the AI next to a public filing or next to a report a portfolio company shared with you. Your account (sign-in, settings, creating a graph) now lives on robosystems.ai, shared with the rest of the product family.

The v0.4.x patch releases went out with bare commit statistics in place of their notes, a release-workflow bug fixed in #294. This file is the first readable account of the series.

## 🔎 Public research on roboinvestor.ai

- **roboinvestor.ai owns the research pages.** `/research` and `/research/{ticker}` are public and rendered on the server, with their own canonical URLs, structured data and sitemap entries, and the old robosystems.ai addresses redirect here. The signed-in research view is gone; the same URL opens the public page, with a bar back to the app (#295, #296)
- **A page for every SEC filer.** Each company in the filer catalog gets a page with a headline strip (revenue, net income, total assets, cash) traced to the filing's XBRL facts, the primary financial statements, and a row per filing linking the viewer, the filing's data files, the document as filed and EDGAR. Companies with research coverage lead with the brief. Foreign private issuers reporting under IFRS show figures in their own currency. The pages are reachable by URL and are not yet listed in the sitemap (#305, #306, #307, #308, #320)
- **Company pages lead with the latest filing.** The page shows the newest filing that carries statements (a 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F or 40-F). On a 10-Q the headline strip reads the quarter, period labels match their span, and the filing is marked "(unaudited)" (#318)
- **A lookup box on `/research`** finds a company by ticker or name (#320)
- **Research pages end on a comparison.** Every page closes with "Connect your books", to put your own company beside the one you just read, with the SEC repository as the second option (#299)
- **An audio edition replaces the podcast.** "Listen to this report" plays a single-voice reading of the brief in the page's own player (#298, #310)
- **Research pages load fast.** The pages are cached at the edge and refresh hourly, and card thumbnails load at card size straight from the CDN instead of being resized on the app server (#309, #314, #315, #323)

## 📊 Company Research in the app

- **`/companies` replaces the SEC filing viewer.** Search every listed filer by ticker or name, or browse the twelve newest briefs. `/companies/{ticker}` shows the brief where one exists, then any filing read whole, with the fact inspector, and `?filing=` keeps your selected filing in the URL. It needs no graph, so it is never locked; the sidebar's Research item leads here (#319)
- **Ask about this filing.** A chat beside the filing puts your question to the AI operator on the SEC repository, anchored on the company and filing on screen. It spends credits from your account, with no key to enter, and is available when your graphs include the SEC repository; otherwise it points you to Repositories (#321)

## 📁 Portfolio reports

- **Ask about a shared report.** The same chat sits on a report a portfolio company shared with you, anchored on the issuer, the period and the report. Each report starts its own thread, and answers come from your graph's copy of the report (#327)

## 👤 Your account lives on RoboSystems

- **Sign-in and registration hand off to robosystems.ai,** which now signs you in across the product family, passkeys included. A failed handoff offers a retry instead of looping (#250, #260)
- **Settings open on robosystems.ai.** The sidebar's settings link opens your RoboSystems settings in a new tab, already signed in, and `/settings` forwards there (#260, #261, #262)
- **Creating a graph keeps your place.** The Create Graph buttons open robosystems.ai in a new tab instead of replacing this one (#263)
- **Docs in the user menu,** linking the platform guides (#325, #326)

## 🔌 Console and MCP

- **The Console answers.** It runs in standard mode, with more tool steps per question and the last three exchanges as context, so a follow-up question works; `/clear` or a graph switch starts fresh. Failures show as errors instead of as answers (#273)
- **Connecting an MCP client starts with sign-in.** Repository Getting Started gives the plain per-repository address for connector clients, and you sign in with the repository already selected. Claude Code and `mcp.json` send the key in a header. The Console's `/mcp` leads with sign-in, and `/mcp key` mints a key scoped to the graph (#267, #268)

## 🌐 Public site

- **The homepage works without JavaScript.** Its content renders on the server instead of arriving as a spinner, it carries one title and description across its metadata, and sitemap dates come only from real changes (#322)
- **Copy that matches the product.** The SEC corpus is described as 8,000+ companies' 10-K, 10-Q, 20-F and 40-F filings. The research console is the Analyst Operator, and the public pages name Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP client (#274, #317, #331)
- The app icons are legible on light backgrounds, and the shared footer links this site's research and the xbrlkit viewer (#296, #297, #301, #311, #324)

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- **Live updates keep working in a tab left open.** Operation progress, streaming queries and Console runs all stopped once a tab outlived its first session refresh, about 25 minutes. They now reconnect, and Console runs fall back to polling if the stream can't open (#276)
- **The landing page fits phones and tablets.** It no longer scrolls sideways on a phone, and the menu, Login and Register are reachable at every width (#257)
- **Quarterly statements show both columns.** A 10-Q's three-month and six-month columns no longer collapse into one, headline figures render on every page again, and headings that only repeat the section title are dropped (#316, #318)
- **No more "Video unavailable."** Research pages that embedded retired podcast videos now carry the audio edition (#298)
- **Structured data is clean.** Each research page has one breadcrumb trail instead of two conflicting ones, and dates carry a time zone (#298, #330)
- Dark-mode table headers are readable in rendered markdown (#283), signing out stays signed out (#252), and search engines are kept off the signed-in Company Research and report pages (#333)

## ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **The SEC filing viewer under Repositories is gone.** `/repositories/{repo}/reports` and its company pages redirect to `/companies`. A deep link to a company lands on the search page, not the company. The sidebar's "Reports" item is removed; Portfolio Reports is unaffected (#319)
- **This app no longer signs users in itself.** `/login` and `/register` always hand off to the RoboSystems login home. A self-hosted deployment needs RoboSystems App running to sign anyone in (#250, #260)
- **`/settings` is no longer a page here.** Profile, password and API-key management live on robosystems.ai/settings. Nothing is lost; it is one app over (#260, #262)
- **Connector URLs with an embedded key are no longer offered,** and the API no longer accepts them. A connection saved that way needs to switch to sign-in, or to a key sent in a header (#267)

## 🔧 Infrastructure

- **`@robosystems/client` 1.8.1 → 1.17.2.** This app uses the facade clients, which were unchanged across the series, so no source changed with the bumps (#253, #254, #255, #269, #275, #276, #285, #286, #332)
- **`@robosystems/core` 0.6.3 → 0.9.5,** carrying the sign-in handoff, the settings handoff, the Console changes, the report chat and the shared footer (#250, #252, #253, #254, #255, #260, #261, #268, #273, #285, #296, #311, #321, #324, #325, #326)
- **`@robosystems/report-components` 0.3.4 → 0.7.0,** bringing the Tavi adapter and the statement-rendering fixes above. 0.7.0's document surface under text blocks is invisible here (#285, #308, #311, #316, #318, #332)
- **Next 16.3,** and the Node 24 base image to 24.19.0. The dev toolchain moves to Vite 8 and `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6. React and TypeScript are unchanged (#265, #278, #284)
- **`npm audit` reports zero.** Overrides were reviewed, with redundant ones dropped and a load-bearing one added. Dependabot now watches the Node base image, and the three frontends' checks are staggered (#264, #284, #287, #289, #290, #312, #313)
- **CI and releases** run on shared workflows from the platform repository: code review, change classification, and the release notes that carry this file. Releases deploy only by dispatch, the production approval gate comes before the tests, and a deploy picks its CloudFormation action from the stack's state, including recovering a stack stuck in rollback. The Docker Hub build runs natively and beside the deploy rather than in front of it (#256, #270, #271, #272, #291, #292, #293, #294, #302, #303, #304)
- **For forks and self-hosters:** `bin/bootstrap.sh` is removed. The deploy role's variables are set by the backend's `just bootstrap` (#300)

## 📦 Deploy notes

- **No API upgrade is required.** Everything in this release is served by API v1.12.8, already in production, and the filer catalog and research media the pages read are already published.
- **No pending CloudFormation changes.** The series added edge cache policies for research pages and images to `cloudformation/template.yaml`, and those already reached production with the v0.4.x patches.
- **One new optional variable,** `NEXT_PUBLIC_FILINGS_CDN_URL`, which defaults to `https://public.robosystems.ai`.
- **Production is sized at 0.5 vCPU and 1 GB** (`CPU_PROD`, `MEMORY_PROD`), set during the series and already live.
